sn6.10:6.1: Is this number meant literally or metaphorically? Assuming that the _khārika_ (“bushel”) here is the _khāri_ of the Arthaśāstra, it is about 150 kg (Olivelle *King, Governance, and Law*, appendix 2, pg. 458; see also note on [sn3.13:1.2]()). Twenty bushels would be 3000 kg, which is reasonable; teams of bullocks regularly pull twice that amount. Estimating one gram of sesame having 500 seeds, a cartload would contain about 1.5 billion seeds. Removing one per century, it would take 150 billion years to empty. This is said to be less than an _abbuda_. However, the _abbuda_ is normally said to be only 10 million or 100 million, though reckonings as high as ten billion as found. Further, as noted below, the length of the Pink Lotus hell yielded by this passage exceeds other calculations, even using the smaller _abbuda_ of 10 million. Thus it seems that this metaphor does not yield the actual number.
sn6.10:6.2: Ten hells are listed here, the names of which do not correspond with the 21 or 28 listed in Purāṇas, nor with the seven Jain hells, nor with the hells of [mn130](). The commentary offers three explanations for the obscure names of these hells: they are numbers reflecting the duration spent in Avīci; or they are the cries uttered by those suffering there; or they are simply the cold hells.
sn6.10:6.3: The Sanskrit _nyarbuda_ is said rather to be ten times the _arbuda_. Normally number sequences in Indian texts multiply by ten, so it seems the “twenty” here is meant to reinforce the greatness of the magnitude.
sn6.10:6.9: The _sogandhika_ is variously identified as blue or white.
sn6.10:6.11: Assuming the smaller _arbuda_ of ten million, the Pink Lotus lasts for 5.12×10¹⁸ years.
sn6.10:10.1: The relations between the numbers in this passage are not clear, but if we follow the grammar suggested by Vanarata, they work out as follows (Bodhi, *Numerical Discourses*, footnote 626 to [an4.3:5.1]()). The commentarial reckoning yields an _abbuda_ of 10⁴², which is way too high. Assuming an _abbuda_ of 10 million, and a _nirabbuda_ of 100 million, we have: 136,000 × 10⁸ = 1.36 × 10¹³ plus 5000 × 10⁷ = 5 × 10¹⁰, totaling 1.365 × 10¹³.
